about.title: La Canada Flintridge Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Product liability cases in La Canada Flintridge don't usually begin at a busy intersection or along the Angeles Crest Highway corridor — they begin at home, in a garage, or on a job site, when a household item, tool, vehicle part, or piece of equipment fails in a way it never should have. Because California generally applies strict liability to defective products, an injured person doesn't have to prove a manufacturer was careless, only that the product itself was defective and that the defect caused harm. That distinction matters in a community like this one, where residents may be dealing with an insurer or a company far outside the area. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent clients directly. We simply listen to what happened, then connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate whether a design flaw, manufacturing error, or missing warning label played a role in your injury.

whyChoose.title: Why La Canada Flintridge Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify the Fight
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to prove a manufacturer was negligent — just that the defect existed and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer who sold the product can potentially be held liable, which widens the field for pursuing a fair outcome.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: An independent attorney can advise you early on how to properly preserve the defective item itself, since it often serves as the central piece of evidence in these claims.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, manuals, or parts that broke off. Don't attempt to repair or discard it, since the product itself is usually the most important evidence in a defect claim. An independent attorney can advise you on safe storage until it's reviewed.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach, you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the company acted carelessly or had knowledge of the problem. This is different from many other types of injury claims.

items.question: I live near the Foothill Boulevard or I-210 corridor in La Canada Flintridge — does that affect my product claim?
items.answer: Where you live doesn't change the legal standard for a product defect claim, but it can affect where you received care and who inspects the product. If the defective item was in your car or involved in an incident near a corridor like Foothill Boulevard or I-210, an attorney will still focus on the product's design, manufacturing, or warnings rather than the road itself.
